answer: An agent economy can require every identity that votes on a settlement to lock a scarce token as collateral, with voting weight capped per identity and rewards released only after a challenge window. A Sybil attacker can create a plume of accounts, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: each must tie up real capital, and disputed votes risk slashing. A bridge can aggregate votes while checking those locks, and a delta in one account’s stake changes only its capped weight, not the others’.
